items.informal_name: Divisibility by $(X - a)^{k}$ for Root Multiplicity $k$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (p : Polynomial R) (a : R),
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p ∣ p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ and any root $ a \in R $, the polynomial $ (X - a)^{k} $, where $ k $ is the multiplicity of $ a $ in $ p $, divides $ p $. This asserts that the factor corresponding to a root raised to its multiplicity is a divisor of the polynomial.

items.informal_name: Polynomial Factorization via Root Multiplicity Equality
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (p : Polynomial R) (a : R),
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p *
      (p /ₘ (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p) =
    p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ and element $ a \in R $, it holds that $ (X - a)^{\operatorname{rootMultiplicity}(a, p)} \cdot \left( p / (X - a)^{\operatorname{rootMultiplicity}(a, p)} \right) = p $.

items.informal_name: Polynomial Factorization with Root Multiplicity and Non-Divisibility
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (p : Polynomial R),
  p ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (a : R),
      ∃ q,
        p = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p * q ∧ ¬Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a ∣ q
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ and element $ a \in R $, there exists a polynomial $ q \in R[X] $ such that $ p = (X - a)^{\operatorname{rootMultiplicity}(a, p)} \cdot q $ and $ (X - a) $ does not divide $ q $.

items.informal_name: Rational Root Theorem: Numerator Divides Constant Term
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → IsFractionRing.num A r ∣ p.coeff 0
items.informal_description: If $ r $ is a root of the polynomial $ p $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of a commutative semiring $ A $, then the numerator of $ r $ divides the constant term $ p(0) $ of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Non-Divisibility by $(X - a)^{m+1}$ for Root Multiplicity $m$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] {p : Polynomial R},
  p ≠ 0 → ∀ (a : R), ¬(Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ (Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p + 1) ∣ p
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $p$ in the polynomial ring $R[X]$ and any element $a \in R$, the polynomial $(X - a)$ raised to the power of the multiplicity $m$ of $a$ as a root of $p$ plus one does not divide $p$.

items.informal_name: Denominator Divides Leading Coefficient for Roots in Fraction Ring
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → ↑(IsFractionRing.den A r) ∣ p.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ A $ and an element $ r $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of $ A $, if $ r $ is a root of $ p $ (i.e., $ \text{aeval}(r, p) = 0 $), then the denominator $ \text{den}(r) $ of $ r $ (as defined in the fraction ring) divides the leading coefficient of $ p $. This generalizes the classical Rational Root Theorem to fraction rings of commutative semirings.

items.informal_name: Rational Root Theorem: Numerator Divides Constant Term
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → IsFractionRing.num A r ∣ p.coeff 0
items.informal_description: If $ r $ is a root of the polynomial $ p $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of a commutative semiring $ A $, then the numerator of $ r $ divides the constant term $ p(0) $ of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Coprime Polynomial and Quotient Given Non-Zero Derivative at Root
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (f : Polynomial K) (a : K),
  Polynomial.eval a (Polynomial.derivative f) ≠ 0 →
    IsCoprime (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) (f /ₘ (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a))
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ f $ over a field $ K $, if $ a $ is a root of $ f $ and the derivative of $ f $ evaluated at $ a $ is non-zero, then the linear polynomial $ X - a $ and the quotient polynomial $ f / (X - a) $ are coprime in $ K[X] $.

items.informal_name: Divisibility by $(X - a)^{k}$ for Root Multiplicity $k$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (p : Polynomial R) (a : R),
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p ∣ p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ and any root $ a \in R $, the polynomial $ (X - a)^{k} $, where $ k $ is the multiplicity of $ a $ in $ p $, divides $ p $. This asserts that the factor corresponding to a root raised to its multiplicity is a divisor of the polynomial.

items.informal_name: Divisibility of Primitive Polynomials via Fraction Ring Extension
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {K : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Field K] [inst_2 : Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
  [IsDomain R] [Nonempty (NormalizedGCDMonoid R)] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.IsPrimitive → q.IsPrimitive → Polynomial.map (algebraMap R K) p ∣ Polynomial.map (algebraMap R K) q → p ∣ q
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring and $ K $ its fraction field. If $ p $ and $ q $ are primitive polynomials in $ R[X] $, and the image of $ p $ under the canonical ring homomorphism $ R \to K $ divides the image of $ q $ in $ K[X] $, then $ p $ divides $ q $ in $ R[X] $.

items.informal_name: Divisibility by Normalized Coprime Polynomial Factor
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] (p : Polynomial K) {q : Polynomial K},
  q ≠ 0 → Polynomial.C (q / gcd p q).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (p / gcd p q) ∣ p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ and non-zero polynomial $ q $ over a field $ K $, the product of the constant polynomial with coefficient equal to the inverse of the leading coefficient of $ q / \gcd(p, q) $ and the polynomial $ p / \gcd(p, q) $ divides $ p $. This constructs a normalized coprime divisor of $ p $ by adjusting the leading coefficient of the coprime part of $ q $.
